case.title: CATL's Debrecen plant: the EU comparison
case.subtitle: Contemporary Amperex Technology Hungary Kft. · Debrecen, Hungary
case.question: Does the same tracing method work for a Chinese-owned battery plant inside the EU, and what would the EU's own rules ask about it?
case.answer: Ownership: yes. Hungarian registry data shows CATL owning the Debrecen plant 100% through its Hong Kong holding company, and China's own investment register agrees. Trade: only partly. Sayari shows seven shipments of Chinese factory equipment and no battery materials or exports, because goods moving inside the EU leave no customs record.
case.why_it_matters: The US rules ask who owns a supplier; the EU rules ask where its raw materials came from. For a CATL plant in the EU the ownership answer is easy to find in registry data. The sourcing answer, which is what the EU will require from 2027, is the part trade data can't see once material crosses an EU border.
case.headline: Inside the EU, the ownership half of the method works well and the trade half goes dark. Sayari traces CATL's Debrecen cell plant to CATL in China through a 100% Hong Kong parent, using the Hungarian registry. But the only shipments it sees are seven loads of Chinese production equipment from 2025. No cathode, anode or cells appear, and nothing goes to the US.
case.summary_for_non_experts: CATL, the world's biggest battery maker, is building a 100 GWh cell factory in Debrecen, Hungary. It started trial cell production on 22 Sep 2026. Hungarian company records in Sayari show the plant belongs to CATL's Hong Kong subsidiary, which CATL owns. Hungarian customs data shows only robots, coating machines, trays and a transformer arriving from China. Inside the EU, goods cross borders without customs paperwork, so supplies from, say, CATL's German plant or an EU anode maker would not show up at all.

steps.title: Choosing the plant
steps.text: We checked three candidates. Shanshan's planned anode plant has a Finnish registry record (in Mustasaari near Vaasa, not Kokkola) but no owner and no trade. Searches for Huayou or BTR companies in Hungary found none. CATL's Debrecen plant had a registry record, an ownership chain, an investment-register entry and customs rows, so it is the one we traced. It makes cells, not anode material.

steps.title: The plant: four records, one company
steps.text: Sayari holds four records for CATL's Hungarian company. The Hungarian registry record carries the company number, tax number and LEI. The other three (a risk-intelligence record, a customs-data fragment and a Chinese investment-register entry) match it by name, so we link them as Inferred or Lead.

steps.title: The owner: two registers agree
steps.text: The Hungarian registry names CATL's Hong Kong holding company as 100% owner. Sayari then links that company to CATL. Separately, China's outbound-investment register lists CATL as the investor in its Hungarian company. Sayari flags CATL as on the US Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies.

steps.title: Inputs: machines, not materials
steps.text: Seven 2025 shipments from Yantian to Budapest name CATL or its Hungarian company: robots, trays, extrusion-coating machine parts and a power transformer (HS 8504.23). CATL usually ships to freight forwarders (Ghibli, DSV), not to the plant by name. The only Chinese artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) entering Hungary goes to the Korean-owned plants of Samsung SDI and SK On.

steps.title: Outputs, and the EU blind spot
steps.text: No shipment naming CATL leaves Hungary. The only Hungary-to-US lithium-ion rows are a forwarder's own 2024 consolidations, with no maker named. Debrecen's cells are meant for European carmakers, and goods moving between EU countries don't go through customs. So the plant's EU customers, and any inputs from EU suppliers, are invisible in trade data.

steps.title: Two rulebooks, two questions
steps.text: The EU Battery Regulation makes battery makers check how cobalt, natural graphite, lithium and nickel were sourced. That duty now starts on 18 Aug 2027, after a two-year delay. From 18 Feb 2027, EV batteries need a digital battery passport. Neither rule asks who owns the supplier. The US PFE rules do ask, and for this plant the registry answer is a 100% Chinese parent.

caveats: Building a battery plant in Hungary with Chinese ownership is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
Debrecen is a cell plant, not an anode plant. We chose it because it had the most Sayari data. The anode-plant candidate (Shanshan, Finland) had a registry record only.
The brief placed Shanshan's plant in Kokkola; registry data and the City of Vaasa put it in Mustasaari (Korsholm), in the GigaVaasa area.
Hungarian customs data covers trade with non-EU countries. Goods moving between EU member states don't go through customs, so intra-EU inputs and sales are missing by design.
Freight forwarders (Ghibli, DSV) are named as consignees. Linking their shipments to the plant is our inference from the goods and timing.
The Section 1260H flag on CATL comes from Sayari. We did not assess how it or CATL's ownership would be treated under the PFE rules; that depends on Treasury guidance.
The policy comparison is limited to the dates and scope stated in the EUR-Lex texts we read (Regulations 2023/1542 and 2025/1561).
Searches for Huayou and BTR companies in Hungary were by name only and limited by budget; a record under another name could exist.
Records checked on 18 Oct 2026. Sayari merges and retires IDs.

params.query: CATL Debrecen battery plant production start 2026

calls.question: What is the status of CATL's Debrecen plant?
calls.result_summary: CATL release (PR Newswire, 22 Sep 2026): trial production of cells began 22 Sep 2026 on the first two lines, after an occupancy permit in Aug 2026; the project was announced Aug 2022 and the first cell building started in summer 2023. iGrow News (23 Sep 2026): first phase 34 GWh, full site planned for 100 GWh; modules made in Debrecen since autumn 2024. CnEVPost (Sep 2025): investment of up to EUR 7.34 bn; about 90% of CATL's May 2025 Hong Kong listing proceeds earmarked for the Hungarian project.
calls.interpretation: The cell plant entered trial production a month ago. It is a company statement plus press coverage.

params.query: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 battery due diligence obligations postponed 2027 battery passport Article 77 Article 48

calls.question: What do the EU Battery Regulation's due-diligence rules cover, and when do they apply?
calls.result_summary: Regulation (EU) 2025/1561 of 18 Jul 2025 (EUR-Lex): Regulation 2023/1542 imposes due-diligence obligations covering the sourcing, processing and trading of cobalt, natural graphite, lithium and nickel; Article 48(1)'s application date moves from 18 Aug 2025 to 18 Aug 2027, and the Commission guidelines date (Art. 48(5)) to 26 Jul 2026. Commission proposal COM(2025)258 gives the reason as time for guidelines and notified bodies.
calls.interpretation: Primary EU source. The duty is about where raw materials come from and how they were produced, not about who owns the supplier.

params.query: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Article 77 battery passport "18 February 2027" electric vehicle batteries

calls.question: When does the EU battery passport apply?
calls.result_summary: EUR-Lex text of Regulation 2023/1542, Article 77(1): from 18 Feb 2027 each LMT battery, industrial battery over 2 kWh and electric-vehicle battery placed on the market must have an electronic 'battery passport'. Article 13(6): from the same date batteries carry a QR code linking to it. Carbon-footprint declarations for EV batteries are phased from 18 Aug 2026 or 18 months after the delegated act, whichever is later.
calls.interpretation: Primary EU source for the passport date.
